title: Sounds a check can prove played, through volatile.audio and the level, in Rust
note: Load sounds in on_reset with gfx.sound, play them through ctx.audio, and prove they played from state().volatile.audio.events and the audio level, never by ear.
intent: Nobody listens to a judged run, so a sound counts only when the state says it played. The template ships [audio] enabled = false, so every sound is missing (audio-disabled) until genex.toml sets [audio] enabled = true: switch it on in the same change that adds the first sound. Load every sound in on_reset with gfx.sound(path) and music with gfx.music(path) (a refused file is a missing handle: sound.refusal() names why and volatile.audio.issues lists it). Play from on_update or the UI hooks with ctx.audio.play(&sound), ctx.audio.play_at(&sound, position) for a sound in the world, and ctx.audio.music(&music, opts) for music; menu sounds use PlayOpts::ui(). To verify a sound: step past the tick that plays it and read state().volatile.audio.events for its played event (and counts.played), or a refused event with its code. The level, audioLevel on a native run and the page's audio() answer on the web, is the game's own mix before the mute: rms above 0 means something sounded; the page's answer counts only when available is true. Audio never enters the checksum, and a headless run never opens a device, so a muted or silent machine still measures.
port: The facet that owns a sound loads and plays it; another facet reads what played from volatile.audio, never from a second copy of the sound.

evidence.note: gfx.sound and gfx.music load in on_reset, ctx.audio plays from the tick, and a refused file is a missing handle whose refusal() says why.
volatile.audio.events lists played, refused and the rest with their tick; audioLevel and the page's audio() answer the game's own mix before the mute.
The page's audio() answers {available, rms, centroid}; available false is never judged.
